# Enhancement Description
- One-line enhancement description: external client-go credential providers
- Kubernetes Enhancement Proposal: [KEP](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/tree/master/keps/sig-auth/541-external-credential-providers)
- Primary contact: @ankeesler

retrieved_evidence.source_fragment:
A new authentication flow in libraries around `kubeconfig` based on
executables. Before performing a request, client executes a binary and uses its
output for authentication.

There are two modes of authentication:

1. Bearer tokens
2. mTLS

Provider response is cached in-memory by the client and reused in future
requests (no caching is done across different executions of the client).  Note
that the executable is free to perform any actions internally (i.e. it may
cache credentials on disk / external hardware, communicate with arbitrary
external APIs, perform arbitrary computations, etc).

Client is configured with a binary path, optional arguments and environment
variables to pass to it.  An optional install hint can be included to help a
user determine how to install an executable if it is missing.  A simple mechanism
is available to handle per cluster configuration.

Configuration is provided via the users and clusters section of `kubeconfig` file:

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Config
users:
- name: my-user
  user:
    exec:
      # API version to use when decoding the ExecCredentials resource. Required.
      apiVersion: "client.authentication.k8s.io/v1"

# Command to execute. Required.
      command: "example-client-go-exec-plugin"

# Arguments to pass when executing the plugin. Optional.
      args:
      - "arg1"
      - "arg2"

# Environment variables to set when executing the plugin. Optional.
      env:
      - name: "FOO"
        value: "bar"

# Text shown to the user when the executable doesn't seem to be present. Optional.
      installHint: |
        example-client-go-exec-plugin is required to authenticate
        to the current cluster.  It can be installed:

On macOS: brew install example-client-go-exec-plugin

On Ubuntu: apt-get install example-client-go-exec-plugin

On Fedora: dnf install example-client-go-exec-plugin

...

# Whether or not to provide cluster information, which could potentially contain
      # very large CA data, to this exec plugin as a part of the KUBERNETES_EXEC_INFO
      # environment variable. Optional. Defaults to false.
      provideClusterInfo: true

# The contract between the exec plugin and the standard input I/O stream. If the
      # contract cannot be satisfied, this plugin will not be run and an error will be
      # returned. Valid values are "Never" (this exec plugin never uses standard input),
      # "IfAvailable" (this exec plugin wants to use standard input if it is available),
      # or "Always" (this exec plugin requires standard input to function).
      #
      # In v1alpha1 and v1beta1, this is optional and defaults to IfAvailable. It is
      # required otherwise.
      interactiveMode: Never
clusters:
- name: my-cluster
  cluster:
    server: "https://1.2.3.4:8080"
    certificate-authority: "/etc/kubernetes/ca.pem"
    extensions:
    - name: client.authentication.k8s.io/exec  # reserved extension name for per cluster exec config
      extension:
        some-config-per-cluster: config-data  # arbitrary config
contexts:
- name: my-cluster
  context:
    cluster: my-cluster
    user: my-user
current-context: my-cluster
```

The Go struct for the `users[...].user.exec` field:

```golang
// ExecConfig specifies a command to provide client credentials. The command is exec'd
// and outputs structured stdout holding credentials.
//
// See the client.authentiction.k8s.io API group for specifications of the exact input
// and output format
type ExecConfig struct {
  // Command to execute.
  Command string `json:"command"`
  // Arguments to pass to the command when executing it.
  // +optional
  Args []string `json:"args"`
  // Env defines additional environment variables to expose to the process. These
  // are unioned with the host's environment, as well as variables client-go uses
  // to pass argument to the plugin.
  // +optional
  Env []ExecEnvVar `json:"env"`

// Preferred input version of the ExecInfo. The returned ExecCredentials MUST use
  // the same encoding version as the input.
  APIVersion string `json:"apiVersion,omitempty"`

// This text is shown to the user when the executable doesn't seem to be
  // present. For example, `brew install foo-cli` might be a good InstallHint for
  // foo-cli on Mac OS systems.
  InstallHint string `json:"installHint,omitempty"`

agent_inferred_risk_findings.description: Exec-based authentication executes an external binary before each request, which can introduce security risks if the binary path is untrusted or compromised. The binary has access to environment variables and potentially cluster information, and its output is used for authentication, making it a vector for credential theft or malicious actions.
agent_inferred_risk_findings.uncertainty: The evidence does not specify how the binary path is validated or whether any sandboxing is applied.

agent_inferred_risk_findings.description: The ExecCredential API transmits sensitive fields such as token, clientKeyData, and clientCertificateData between the client and exec plugin. The evidence notes these should only be transmitted in-memory, but if the plugin is compromised or the communication channel is not secure, credentials could be exposed.
agent_inferred_risk_findings.uncertainty: The evidence does not detail the exact in-memory transmission mechanism or potential side-channel leaks.

agent_inferred_risk_findings.description: Caching of provider response in-memory until expirationTimestamp, or for the client runtime if no expiration is set, can lead to stale credentials being used if the expiration is not properly set or if the client runs for a long time. This could result in authentication failures or unauthorized access if credentials are revoked before expiration.
agent_inferred_risk_findings.uncertainty: The evidence does not specify how expirationTimestamp is validated or what happens if the plugin returns an invalid timestamp.

agent_inferred_risk_findings.description: The new configuration fields in kubeconfig (exec section) introduce complexity and potential backward compatibility issues. Existing kubeconfig files that do not include these fields may behave differently, and the required interactiveMode field in newer API versions could break older plugins that do not set it.
agent_inferred_risk_findings.uncertainty: The evidence does not specify migration paths or versioning strategies for existing kubeconfig users.

agent_inferred_risk_findings.description: Error handling for exec plugin execution is critical: if the binary is missing, fails to execute, or returns invalid output, the client must handle it gracefully. The installHint is provided for missing binaries, but other errors (e.g., invalid JSON, wrong API version) may not be well-handled, leading to authentication failures or crashes.
agent_inferred_risk_findings.uncertainty: The evidence does not detail the exact error handling behavior for various failure modes.

agent_inferred_risk_findings.description: The new metrics for exec plugin calls, certificate TTL, and rotation age may be incorrect if the exec plugin does not provide accurate expirationTimestamp or if the client caches credentials beyond the actual certificate validity. This could lead to misleading metrics and operational issues.
agent_inferred_risk_findings.uncertainty: The evidence does not specify how metrics are collected or validated.

agent_inferred_risk_findings.description: Deprecation of gcp and azure authentication options (and keystone already deprecated) may break existing users who rely on these methods. agent_inferred_risk_findings.uncertainty: The evidence does not provide details on the deprecation timeline or migration support.

test_plans.content:
### Test Plan

Unit tests to confirm:

- Version mismatch is detected
- Credentials are cached in-memory correctly
  + Executable is only called as needed
  + Expired credentials are rotated automatically
  + Credentials are used across many requests (as long as they are still valid)
- Single flight all calls to a given executable (when the config is the same)
- Reasonable timeout to executable calls so clients do not hang indefinitely
- `"k8s.io/client-go/pkg/apis/clientauthentication".Cluster` (and external types)
  fields (Go and JSON) properly shadow
  `"k8s.io/client-go/tools/clientcmd/api/v1".Cluster` fields (with the exception of
  `CertificateAuthority` for reasons stated in design) so
  that structs are kept up to date
- Helper methods properly create `"k8s.io/client-go/rest".Config` from
  `"k8s.io/client-go/pkg/apis/clientauthentication".Cluster` and vice versa
- Metrics are reported as they should

Integration (or e2e CLI) tests to confirm:

- Shared informers backed by exec credential work as expected
  + Credential rotation does not cause issues
  + Transient failures are correctly retried
  + Executables requiring interactive prompts fail gracefully
  + Executables are not called in a hot loop during transient failure
- Static forms of auth should interact correctly with exec credential plugin
  + Basic auth
  + Token based auth
  + Cert based auth
- Interactive login flows work
  + TTY forwarding between client and executable works
  + `kubectl` commands and exec credential plugins do not fight for standard input
  + All `InteractiveMode` values are supported
- Metrics are reported as they should

value.coverage_assessment: The existing test plan covers key aspects of the exec-based authentication flow, including version mismatch detection, in-memory caching, single-flight behavior, timeouts, struct shadowing, helper methods, metrics, integration with shared informers, static auth interactions, and interactive login flows. However, the plan is high-level and lacks specific test cases for security, error handling, and backward compatibility. The absence of concrete test cases means the plan may not be fully implemented or validated.
potential_gaps: Security of credentials: no explicit tests for credential handling in memory, output masking, or prevention of credential leakage in logs or error messages.
Execution of external binaries: no tests for handling malicious or malformed executable output, command injection via args/env, or validation of executable path.
Backward compatibility: no tests for existing kubeconfig files without exec sections, or for deprecated gcp/azure auth options still functioning.
Error handling: no tests for non-zero exit codes, missing executable, permission denied, or malformed ExecCredential responses.
Stale credentials: no tests for expirationTimestamp in the past, or for caching behavior when expiration is absent.
Metric correctness: no tests for metric labels, values, or emission timing for exec plugin calls, certificate TTL, and rotation age.
Interactive mode: no tests for all InteractiveMode values (Never, IfAvailable, Always) and their fallback behavior.
Cluster information: no tests for provideClusterInfo=true and the content of spec.cluster, including CA data handling.
Concurrency: no tests for concurrent requests with different exec configs or for single-flight behavior under high concurrency.
Timeout: no tests for configurable timeout or for handling executables that hang indefinitely.
recommended_missing_cases: Test that credentials are not logged or exposed in error messages or metrics.
Test that executable output is validated against the ExecCredential schema and that invalid output is rejected.
Test that command injection via args or env is not possible (e.g., using shell metacharacters).
Test that deprecated gcp and azure auth options still work and produce deprecation warnings.
Test that kubeconfig files without exec sections continue to work without regression.
Test that non-zero exit codes from the executable result in clear errors and no credential caching.
Test that missing executable or permission denied errors are handled gracefully and do not crash the client.
Test that expirationTimestamp in the past causes immediate rotation and that no expiration leads to caching for the client runtime.
Test that metrics for exec plugin calls, certificate TTL, and rotation age are emitted with correct labels and values.
Test all InteractiveMode values (Never, IfAvailable, Always) and verify fallback behavior when TTY is not available.
Test that provideClusterInfo=true populates spec.cluster correctly, including CA data and server address.
Test that concurrent requests with different exec configs do not interfere and that single-flight works per config.
Test that a configurable timeout is applied to executable calls and that hanging executables are killed.
Test that transient failures during credential rotation are retried without hot-looping the executable.
Test that static auth (basic, token, cert) can be combined with exec credential and that exec takes precedence when configured.

# Feature Risk Review

## Feature Summary

This feature introduces external credential providers for Kubernetes client authentication, allowing out-of-tree executables to supply credentials (bearer tokens or mTLS) via a new exec-based authentication flow. It defines configuration in kubeconfig, input/output formats (ExecCredential), caching behavior, and metrics for monitoring.

## Change Points

- New exec-based authentication flow in client libraries: before each request, the client executes a configured binary and uses its output for authentication.
- Addition of new configuration fields in kubeconfig (exec section) for users, including command, args, env, installHint, provideClusterInfo, and interactiveMode.
- New ExecCredential API (client.authentication.k8s.io/v1) with input and output formats, including spec.cluster for cluster information and status for credentials.
- Caching of provider response in-memory until expirationTimestamp; if no expiration, cache for client runtime.
- New metrics for exec plugin calls, certificate TTL, and rotation age.
- Deprecation of gcp and azure authentication options (keystone already deprecated).

## High-Risk Scenarios

- Caching of provider response in-memory until expirationTimestamp, or for the client runtime if no expiration is set, can lead to stale credentials being used if the expiration is not properly set or if the client runs for a long time. This could result in authentication failures or unauthorized access if credentials are revoked before expiration. [C1][C2]
  - Risk area: stale credentials
  - Affected components: client-go, authentication libraries
- Error handling for exec plugin execution is critical: if the binary is missing, fails to execute, or returns invalid output, the client must handle it gracefully. The installHint is provided for missing binaries, but other errors (e.g., invalid JSON, wrong API version) may not be well-handled, leading to authentication failures or crashes. [C3][C4]
  - Risk area: error handling
  - Affected components: client-go, authentication libraries
- Exec-based authentication executes an external binary before each request, which can introduce security risks if the binary path is untrusted or compromised.   - Risk area: security of credentials
  - Affected components: client-go, authentication libraries
- The new configuration fields in kubeconfig (exec section) introduce complexity and potential backward compatibility issues. Existing kubeconfig files that do not include these fields may behave differently, and the required interactiveMode field in newer API versions could break older plugins that do not set it. [C3][C4]
  - Risk area: backward compatibility
  - Affected components: kubeconfig, client-go
- Deprecation of gcp and azure authentication options (and keystone already deprecated) may break existing users who rely on these methods. - The ExecCredential API transmits sensitive fields such as token, clientKeyData, and clientCertificateData between the client and exec plugin.
